item.title: China issues ethical guidelines for AI medical imaging
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-29
BEIJING, Aug. 29 (Xinhua) -- China has released ethical guidelines for artificial intelligence (AI) medical imaging research, aiming to regulate algorithm development, trial verification and clinical application of this technology, the Ministry of Science and Technology said on Friday. AI medical imaging uses AI technology to analyze CT, Magnetic Resonance Imaging and ultrasound scans, assisting doctors in detecting lesions and improving diagnostic efficiency. However, the technology involves large amounts of sensitive health data and carries risks, such as privacy breaches, algorithmic bias and unclear accountability. The guidelines, released by the medical ethics subcommittee of the national science and technology ethics committee, outline six core principles: enhancing human welfare, promoting fairness, respecting human autonomy, protecting privacy and data security, ensuring safety and controllability, and strengthening transparency. Patients' health interests are prioritized, the guidelines noted. The guidelines require researchers to obtain informed consent from participants, and participants have the right to withdraw their authorization at any time. Human beings remain the ultimate accountable entities. AI outputs shall not be used as final diagnoses, and doctors retain the final decision-making authority, according to the guidelines. The guidelines also prohibit exaggerating model performance and underscore the importance of algorithmic fairness, to reduce diagnostic bias caused by imbalanced training samples. ■

item.title: Major Chinese river-to-sea canal passes completion acceptance
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-29
NANNING, Aug. 29 (Xinhua) -- Pinglu Canal in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region has passed its completion acceptance, moving a step closer to its planned opening to navigation in September, the Pinglu Canal Group said on Friday. The acceptance committee, comprising representatives from the regional transport department, maritime safety administration and the canal group, unanimously agreed that the waterway alignment, lock structures, slope protection and ecological embankments all meet design and technical specifications, and that project documentation is complete and well-managed. The 134.2-km canal is a major project along the country's New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, a strategic route linking China's inland regions with ASEAN and other global markets. The project began construction on Aug. 28, 2022, and is expected to become operational next month. ■

item.title: Lolana Lens | How "stroll-and-eat" is reshaping brick-and-mortar retail in China
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-29
Across China, going out to shop is becoming about more than what you put in your shopping cart. From pop-up markets and reinvented supermarkets to new neighborhood commercial spaces, brick-and-mortar retail is finding new ways to bring shopping, leisure and everyday life closer together. What looks like a simple "stroll-and-eat" routine is part of a broader shift in how people shop, spend time and live in cities.

item.title: Factbox: Latest relief and rescue progress at Xizang's mudslide-hit border port
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-29
BEIJING, Aug. 29 (Xinhua) -- A fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse on the Nepalese side, has caused heavy casualties and left many missing at a port on the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. Rescuers immediately launched an all-out effort to reach the mudslide-hit port and search for the missing. Here is what we know about the deadly mudslide and the latest rescue and relief progress there: -- As of 1 a.m. on Saturday, seven people were confirmed dead and 554 others remained missing at Gyirong Port, according to Xizang's emergency management department. -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, on Friday chaired a Party leadership meeting to deliberate and make arrangements on rescue and relief efforts. Every effort should be made to search for and rescue all missing Chinese and foreign nationals, the meeting stressed, adding that China will provide emergency aid to the disaster-hit area in Nepal and carry out international rescue cooperation. -- Premier Li Qiang inspected the damage and met with rescue workers. He called for swift repairs to damaged infrastructure, including roads, communications and power facilities, to restore access for rescue operations as soon as possible. -- At about 4:30 p.m. on Friday, a six-member team from the Xizang Fire and Rescue Corps and a group of 15 members with a search dog from the Sichuan Fire and Rescue Corps arrived at Gyirong Port, becoming the first professional rescue teams to reach the core rescue area, the National Fire and Rescue Administration said. -- More than 500 personnel from the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) and the People's Armed Police Force, along with vehicles and military helicopters, have been deployed in the rescue operations. The first supply truck from the PLA Xizang Military Command has transported more than 9,000 items, including cotton tents, folding beds, and moisture-proof mats, to Gyirong Township. -- China Anneng, a state-owned engineering and rescue enterprise, sent out a 15-member team on Friday with reconnaissance drones, portable satellite stations and mobile surveillance cameras to conduct on-site surveys of the blockage and surrounding roads to provide accurate data for efforts to address the barrier lake. -- Relief operations remain severely hampered by complex and dangerous conditions on the ground, including dangers posed by an upstream barrier lake, heavy downpour, and cut-off roads and communication to the core area. Xinhua reporters at the scene said the mudslide has devastated the river valley below. The silt layer in the core disaster area is more than 1.5 meters deep, posing a high risk of trapping anyone caught in it. -- A total of 499 villagers and construction workers have been properly accommodated. Meanwhile, 555 affected tourists were evacuated and transferred under the coordination of cultural and tourism authorities. No tourists remain stranded. -- The National Commission for Disaster Prevention, Reduction and Relief, together with the Ministry of Emergency Management (MEM), helped allocate 30,000 central relief supplies, including tents, stoves, clothing, quilts, folding beds and moisture-proof mats, to support evacuation, resettlement and relief work. -- The Ministry of Finance and the MEM also allocated 120 million yuan (about 17.7 million U.S. dollars) in central natural disaster relief funds to support Xizang in carrying out emergency rescue and disaster relief operations. ■

item.title: China Focus: South China's Greater Bay Area deepens integration through tech collaboration
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-29
GUANGZHOU, Aug. 29 (Xinhua) -- About 30 years ago, when Hong Kong businessmen came to Dongguan, less than 100 kilometers away in the Pearl River Delta, they invested in the production of toys, clothing, and other low-value-added items that earned the city the nickname "world factory." Today, scientists and young entrepreneurs in Hong Kong are once again heading to Dongguan, now an emerging innovative hub in south China's Guangdong Province, in search of research equipment and experienced talent. This is more than a story of Dongguan's industrial upgrading. Across China's nine Pearl River Delta cities and two special administrative regions, which make up the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, collaboration among enterprises, universities, and research facilities has grown at an unprecedented pace. It has been fueled by technological innovation needs and supportive policies. RESEARCH COOPERATION Since the term of Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area was first mentioned in China's government work report in 2017, a series of experimental facilities and research institutions have been put into operation in the Pearl River Delta, enabling easier access for Hong Kong and Macao researchers to resources that were previously less available. In Dongguan, one of the most iconic facilities is the China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) owned by the Institute of High Energy Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, located near Songshan Lake on the city's outskirts. Following Britain, the United States and Japan, the CSNS is the world's fourth pulsed neutron source facility, and the first in China. Spallation Neutron Source (SNS) is regarded as a more efficient and safe way to produce neutrons -- which are highly useful to material probes -- by using a process that sends high-energy ions into a heavy metal target. For researchers based in Hong Kong and Macao, the CSNS has also become the closest facility to carry out material-related experiments since it began operation in 2018. "We have cooperated with the University of Hong Kong, the City University of Hong Kong (CityUHK), the University of Macau and several other universities in the two regions, which followed the same process as mainland institutions in applying to use the facility," said Tong Xin, deputy director of the Spallation Neutron Source Science Center. According to the center, researchers with seven Hong Kong and Macao universities have so far used the CSNS to conduct 131 research projects in fields such as high-entropy alloys, lithium-battery materials, polymer films and biomedicine. The center also worked with Dongguan University of Technology and CityUHK to build China's first multi-physics spectrometer, which began operation in 2021 for use in various fields of materials science. In 2024, it signed agreements with eight universities in Hong Kong and Macao to jointly build the Southern Advanced Light Source. This synchrotron radiation light source can produce intense beams of light that enable detailed material probing. "We expect to see the Southern Advanced Light Source operate complementarily with the CSNS in micro material probing, better serving the development of the Greater Bay Area," Tong said. TECHNOLOGY COMMERCIALIZATION As a close partner of the CSNS, CityUHK has worked with the Dongguan government to set up a new university near the facility in the Songshan Lake area. City University of Hong Kong (Dongguan), or CityUHK (Dongguan), was officially established in 2024. One reason behind CityUHK's cooperation with Dongguan is the city's exceptional capacity to commercialize technologies from its strong manufacturing base, said Chiu Chi-yue, vice president of CityUHK (Dongguan). "CityUHK has been leading Hong Kong universities in terms of the number of patents. At the same time, the commercialization of patents is not always easy in Hong Kong, but is relatively convenient here in Dongguan," he said. Chiu noted that CityUHK (Dongguan) currently offers five undergraduate programs and 10 master's programs, including materials science and engineering, artificial intelligence (AI), and data science. All are of strategic importance for the development of the Greater Bay Area and the country. Compared with traditional universities, CityUHK (Dongguan) places particular emphasis on fostering innovation and entrepreneurship, encouraging students to participate in faculty-led research early in their university studies. Nearby, the university has found a perfect partnership with Xbot Park, a startup incubator in the Songshan Lake area, which has developed into an industrial cluster spanning research and commercialization. Drawing on the Greater Bay Area's integrated supply chain, Xbot Park, established in 2014, has set up a so-called "shared factory." It collaborates with supply-chain service providers to offer startups support in trial production, project management, and other stages from an initial idea to mass production. "The shared factory helps address core challenges facing startups, such as limited access to supply chains and weak bargaining power," said Yu Chunhua, who is in charge of Xbot Park's supply chain division. The incubator has attracted innovative startups and companies across the Greater Bay Area. CYC Group, a Hong Kong company that develops electronic bikes, opened an office there in 2023. Founder and CEO Jon Chan said the Dongguan office puts the company's supply chain close at hand and makes it possible to hire experienced engineers from the mainland -- talent that is now hard to find in Hong Kong. According to Gao Min, dean of the Guangzhou HKUST Fok Ying Tung Research Institute, professional experimental laboratories and an abundant pool of skilled engineers are among the mainland's key advantages in helping Hong Kong and Macao commercialize technologies. Founded by the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology in Nansha in 2007, the institute was Guangzhou's first scientific research institution with a Hong Kong background. It is currently the university's major mainland-based platform for technology innovation and commercialization. "Only on the mainland can we find highly capable, yet not prohibitively expensive, engineers, who are demanded in large numbers for turning an original technology into an outstanding product," Gao said. OVERSEAS CONNECTION Meanwhile, research and production collaboration with partners in Hong Kong and Macao is helping enterprises in the Pearl River Delta expand more smoothly into overseas markets, according to local business leaders. Guangzhou Pharmaceutical Holdings Limited, a leading traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) manufacturer, has set up a joint laboratory with the University of Macau and a factory in Macao. It also plans to build a modern TCM manufacturing center on Hengqin island in Zhuhai adjacent to Macao. "The Hengqin facility will apply the most advanced international production standards to ensure its products are qualified for Hong Kong and Macao markets, and we hope they can subsequently reach Portuguese-speaking countries and other overseas markets," said Chen Jiehui, vice chairperson and general manager of the enterprise. PCI Technology Group Co., LTD. (PCITECH), a Guangzhou-based enterprise that provides AI solutions for urban traffic management, established an R&D center in Hong Kong at the beginning of this year. Wang Yuemiao, executive director of PCITECH's central research institute, said the center will be responsible for their products' adaptation to international technical standards and development for overseas markets, and serve as a platform to connect cooperation resources and expand markets. Wang said that for mainland companies, Hong Kong can help them connect with overseas markets more efficiently with its mature international business networks and well-developed services in areas such as law, finance, and accounting. Hong Kong also has the strength in helping companies adapt technologies and solutions already proven in China to international standards as well as regulations and business models in foreign markets, he said. "This will help projects realize long-term operations after entering overseas markets." Yet Wang believes that mainland enterprises should see Hong Kong as more than a gateway. Instead, they should bring in the technological, industrial and application capabilities they have developed on the mainland and combine them with Hong Kong's strengths in research, internationalization and professional services. "The goal is to actually integrate the mainland's industrial strengths with Hong Kong's international advantages, so that we can jointly build innovation capacity for global markets," he said. ■

item.title: Shenzhou-23 astronauts complete first series of extravehicular activities
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
This screen image captured at Beijing Aerospace Control Center on Aug. 28, 2026 shows Shenzhou-23 astronaut Zhu Yangzhu performing extravehicular activities outside China's orbiting space station. The Shenzhou-23 crew aboard China's orbiting space station completed their mission's first series of extravehicular activities on Friday, according to the China Manned Space Agency. (Photo by Yu Liqiang/Xinhua) BEIJING, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- The Shenzhou-23 crew aboard China's orbiting space station completed their mission's first series of extravehicular activities on Friday, according to the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA). The astronaut trio -- Zhu Yangzhu, Zhang Zhiyuan and Li Jiaying -- worked for approximately 5.5 hours and completed their tasks at 1:59 p.m. (Beijing Time), assisted by the space station's robotic arm and ground support teams. Zhu, who previously spacewalked three years ago, made his second excursion, while Zhang ventured outside for the first time. Zhu and Zhang installed debris shields and repaired the station's solar panels, ensuring the safety and stability of its power supply, according to the CMSA. This is the second time Chinese astronauts have performed such in-orbit maintenance tasks. The three astronauts were launched aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft on May 24. Since arriving at the station, the crew has completed an in-orbit handover, deployed application payloads outside the station, and conducted rendezvous-and-docking drills, medical rescue exercises and full-system pressure emergency response drills, according to the agency. Scientific experiments and technology tests in space life sciences, human research, microgravity physics and new space technologies are progressing steadily, the CMSA said. In the coming months, they will carry out scientific experiments, technology tests, application payload deployments outside the station, and public outreach activities, the agency added. ■ This screen image captured at Beijing Aerospace Control Center on Aug. 28, 2026 shows Shenzhou-23 astronaut Zhu Yangzhu performing extravehicular activities outside China's orbiting space station. item.title: China helps SCO evolve into comprehensive cooperation platform, says Tajik economist
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
DUSHANBE, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- China is helping transform the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) from a security-focused regional body into a comprehensive platform -- one spanning economy, technology, transport and finance, a Tajik economist said. In an interview with Xinhua, Rahmon Ulmasov, a professor at the Russian-Tajik (Slavonic) University, described China's 2024-2025 rotating presidency as one of the most productive periods in the SCO history. During its presidency, China hosted over 200 events, issued 92 outcome documents, and put forward 36 major cooperation initiatives, Ulmasov noted. "The SCO has gone beyond being solely a regional platform and is gaining global significance." China has become one of SCO's primary economic engines, said Ulmasov, highlighting SCO leaders' approval of a development strategy for the organization in the 2026-2035 period and the member states' decision to establish an SCO development bank at the SCO summit held last year in China's port city of Tianjin. These measures are particularly important for Central Asia, where there is significant demand for financing in transport, energy, water management and digital infrastructure, he said, noting that once the bank becomes fully operational, it could provide countries in the region with new sources of long-term financing. On the logistics front, Ulmasov said that Belt and Road cooperation on infrastructure is fostering closer transport, trade and logistics links among SCO member states, particularly in Central Asia. New cross-border routes are transforming Central Asia from a landlocked area in the Eurasian transport grid into a dynamic hub connecting East and West, as well as North and South, he said. The China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway could also become a new driver of regional economic development, said the Tajik expert. The project is designed to create a new land route connecting China and Central Asia and shorten the existing China-Europe route by about 900 km, providing an alternative to traditional transport routes. Looking ahead, Ulmasov said the SCO is embarking on a new development stage with cooperation expanding beyond traditional trade, transport and conventional energy to technological modernization in green energy, artificial intelligence, the digital economy and emerging industries. China is aligning its own modernization drive with the development needs of fellow SCO member states, creating a new model of cooperation that combines Chinese technology, local resources, joint production and access to regional markets, he said. China, he said, is offering SCO members more than a share in its economic momentum; it is offering a way into the high-tech supply chains of the future. As these initiatives take root, he added, the SCO could become a premier hub for the region's green and digital economic transformation.■

item.title: China passes healthcare security law, appoints civil affairs minister, ratifies extradition treaty with Hungary
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
Zhao Leji, chairman of the National People's Congress (NPC) Standing Committee, presides over the closing meeting of the 24th session of the 14th NPC Standing Committee at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 28, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Weibing) BEIJING, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- Chinese lawmakers on Friday voted to adopt a new healthcare security law, approve the appointment of a new civil affairs minister, and ratify an extradition treaty with Hungary. The votes were taken at a closing meeting of the 24th session of the Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress (NPC) in Beijing. Lawmakers also voted to adopt a law on farmland protection and quality improvement, a revised Agriculture Law, a revised National Defense Mobilization Law, and a decision on amending the lawyers law. They also adopted a decision to remove Lu Zhiyuan from the post of minister of civil affairs, and appoint Li Changguan as minister of civil affairs. President Xi Jinping signed five presidential orders to promulgate the laws and the decision, and a sixth one to announce the decision on the personnel change. Zhao Leji, chairman of the NPC Standing Committee, presided over the closing meeting. In the meeting, lawmakers ratified an extradition treaty between China and Hungary. The legislature voted to remove Zhang Youxia as vice chairman of the Central Military Commission (CMC) of the People's Republic of China and Liu Zhenli as a member of the CMC. Lawmakers also voted on several personnel appointments and removals and other personnel-related bills. They also passed a deputy qualification report. While addressing the closing meeting, Zhao said that legislative work should place greater emphasis on safeguarding and promoting social fairness and justice, further improve the socialist legal system with Chinese characteristics, and provide solid legal guarantees for advancing Chinese modernization on all fronts. He stressed the need to strengthen legislation in key, emerging and foreign-related fields, and called for efforts to improve the quality of legislation and ensure that it keeps pace with changing needs. Zhao also chaired a meeting of the Council of Chairpersons of the NPC Standing Committee before the closing meeting, and presided over a lecture for lawmakers afterward. ■

item.title: Xi chairs CPC leadership meeting on Gyirong County mudslide rescue efforts
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
BEIJING, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on Friday chaired a Party leadership meeting to deliberate and make arrangements on rescue and relief efforts after a devastating mudslide hit Gyirong County in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. At the beginning of the meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, Xi, who is also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, and other leaders, including Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, observed a moment of silence to mourn the victims of the disaster. A mudslide in Nepal on Wednesday struck the border port of Gyirong, causing heavy casualties and leaving many people missing. Following the disaster, the CPC Central Committee attached great importance to the situation, and Xi immediately issued important instructions on rescue and emergency response efforts. Entrusted by Xi, Premier Li Qiang, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, traveled to the disaster-hit area to visit the affected people and rescue and relief personnel, and to supervise rescue and emergency response efforts. Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, also went to the site to guide the response. According to the meeting, emergency rescue operations have been carried out swiftly and in an orderly and well-coordinated manner under the strong leadership of the Party Central Committee, with comprehensive efforts underway for the resettlement of affected people and handling of the aftermath. The disaster occurred in a severely cold plateau region with steep valleys, variable weather, many surrounding glaciers and glacial lakes, as well as potential geological hazards, which poses significant challenges to emergency rescue operations. The meeting emphasized that all relevant authorities and departments must take resolute and effective measures for the rescue-related work. Search and rescue plans should be formulated in a scientific manner, and every effort should be made to search for and rescue all missing Chinese and foreign nationals, it stressed. Multi-department joint consultation must be strengthened, monitoring and early warning enhanced, barrier lake and surrounding mountain stability closely tracked, and effective measures taken to strictly prevent secondary disasters, according to the meeting. It also urged enhancing on-site personnel management to ensure safety throughout the rescue process. China will provide emergency aid to the disaster-hit area in Nepal and carry out international rescue cooperation, the meeting said. The meeting called for conducting comprehensive inspections to identify potential risks and hazards, boosting real-time monitoring and early warning, and enhancing the capacity to identify risks arising from disaster chains. It also urged that emergency response mechanisms should be improved, and key rescue forces be strengthened. More rescue and emergency response forces should be deployed to remote and disaster-prone areas, according to the meeting. International cooperation on disaster management in border areas should also be strengthened to jointly enhance emergency management as well as disaster prevention, mitigation and relief, it added. On better coordinating development and security, the meeting emphasized the need to prepare for worst-case and extreme scenarios, bear a strong sense of political responsibility and constant vigilance, and make solid efforts to ensure safety and stability. ■

item.title: Full text of Xi's signed article in Kyrgyz media
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
BEIJING, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday published a signed article titled "Jointly Opening up New Prospects for the High-Quality Development of China-Kyrgyzstan Relations" in the Slovo Kyrgyzstana and the Kabar National News Agency ahead of his arrival in Kyrgyzstan for a state visit and attendance at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 in Bishkek. The following is the full text of the article: Jointly Opening up New Prospects for the High-Quality Development of China-Kyrgyzstan Relations H.E. Xi Jinping President of the People's Republic of China For Slovo Kyrgyzstana and Kabar National News Agency Early autumn brings clear skies and crisp air. In this season of harvest, I will pay a state visit to Kyrgyzstan and attend the 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) at the invitation of President Sadyr Zhaparov. It will be my third visit to this beautiful land. I look forward to working with President Zhaparov to map out a new blueprint for China-Kyrgyzstan relations and make new progress in building an SCO community with a shared future. This year marks the 35th anniversary of Kyrgyzstan's independence. On behalf of the Chinese government and people, I extend sincere congratulations and best wishes to the friendly people of Kyrgyzstan. We are truly delighted to see our friendly neighbor enjoy sustained political stability, economic growth, and social harmony. China and Kyrgyzstan are good neighbors sharing weal and woe, good partners with a shared future, and good friends who help each other succeed. Our two countries share a long history of exchanges. The ancient Silk Road is a testimony to the long-standing friendship between the two peoples. In both countries, the stories of historical figures such as Zhang Qian, Xuanzang and Li Bai -- who had contributed to civilizational exchanges between China and Kyrgyzstan -- are still widely told. Since the establishment of diplomatic relations, our two countries have always upheld mutual respect, good-neighborliness, mutual learning, and mutual benefit, and steadily deepened mutual trust and cooperation. Having stood the test of changing international circumstances, our bilateral ties have made historic leaps from good-neighborly relations to strategic partnership, and then to comprehensive strategic partnership for the new era, gaining fresh dynamism with each stage of development. In February 2025, President Zhaparov and I reached important common understandings on further deepening the comprehensive strategic partnership for the new era and building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future defined by good-neighborliness, friendship and shared prosperity. The decision opened a new chapter of bilateral relations. -- With mutual trust as our bedrock, we have given each other firm support. Both sides have consistently backed each other in safeguarding sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity, and in adopting policies and measures for national development, thus setting a fine example of good-neighborliness and mutual success for neighboring countries. President Zhaparov and I met three times last year, and we have developed deep trust in each other, both professionally and personally. Together, we are steering China-Kyrgyzstan ties toward greater progress. -- With mutual benefit as our driving force, we have delivered real benefits to our people. China and Kyrgyzstan have complementary economies and immense cooperation potential. Despite sluggish global growth, our business cooperation has continued to make steady progress. China has been Kyrgyzstan's largest trading partner and largest source of foreign investment for many years running. Chinese smart phones and electric vehicles have become trendy choices for Kyrgyz consumers, while more and more quality Kyrgyz farm products are making their way into Chinese kitchens. The two sides have worked together on a number of projects that deliver long-term benefits and real improvements to the lives of local communities. Construction on the Kyrgyz section of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is advancing in full swing, the Bedel checkpoint has been temporarily opened prior to full operation, and direct flights between our two countries are growing. In short, a multimodal connectivity network is increasingly taking shape. -- With heart-to-heart communication as our bridge, we have kept up vibrant exchanges and mutual learning. China has set up one Luban Workshop, four Confucius Institutes, and 21 Confucius Classrooms in Kyrgyzstan, making it easier for local people to acquire vocational skills and learn Chinese. China's "Brightness Journey of Lifeline Express" for cataract patients and traditional Chinese medicine center have brought the benefits of bilateral medical and health cooperation to more people in Kyrgyzstan. The two sides have signed an agreement to set up cultural centers in each other's countries, held cultural days, film festivals, and art festivals, and worked together to protect and promote world intangible cultural heritage like the Manas epic, bringing the charm of each culture closer to the other's people. Two-way visits exceeded 400,000 last year, and 30 pairs of sister provinces and cities enjoy close ties, cementing the foundation for lasting friendship. -- With justice on our side, we have jointly navigated risks and challenges. Linked by mountains and rivers and bound by shared security, China and Kyrgyzstan are staunch defenders of regional security and stability. As founding members of the SCO as well as Global South countries, we share similar positions on upholding international fairness and justice and promoting open, inclusive development. Amid changing and volatile international and regional landscapes, we coordinate closely in multilateral frameworks, actively support each other's major initiatives, and jointly advance an equal and orderly multipolar world and a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization. This year marks the 105th anniversary of the founding of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the launch of China's 15th Five-Year Plan for economic and social development. Under the strong leadership of the CPC, the Chinese people are striding forward confidently and resolutely toward the ambitious goal of building a great modern socialist country in all respects and realizing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The people of Kyrgyzstan are implementing the country's National Development Program until 2030 and making all-out efforts to build a "New Kyrgyzstan." At this new starting point, the two sides should make steady progress toward building the China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future to bring more benefits to the two peoples and contribute even more to regional and world peace, stability, and prosperity. We need to solidify good-neighborliness and friendship. The Chinese people like to say that good neighbors wish each other well, just as loved ones do. China and Kyrgyzstan should always support each other's development, maintain the sound momentum of high-level exchanges and multitiered cooperation, better synergize development strategies, and deepen experience sharing on governance, to provide a solid foundation for each other's development and revitalization. China will continue to do its best to support Kyrgyzstan in growing its economy and improving people's lives. We need to pursue mutual benefit and win-win results. This is essential for the enduring vitality of our cooperation. We should take a long-term view, focus on high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, and continuously upgrade practical cooperation. While strengthening existing cooperation in trade and investment, connectivity, and green mining, we should also cooperate in the digital economy, clean energy, artificial intelligence, and other emerging fields. We need to move forward with building the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, accelerate the revamping of land ports, and advance institutional connectivity alongside physical connectivity to facilitate the smooth flow of people and goods. We need to carry forward the traditional friendship. Our long-standing friendship is an invaluable asset. We should step up exchanges and cooperation in culture, tourism, art, media, think tank, youth, archaeology, and health to forge closer bonds. We should encourage our young people to study in each other's countries and support more substantive outcomes from subnational exchanges. We need to spread the stories of our friendly exchanges and mutually beneficial cooperation to cement the foundation of people-to-people goodwill. We need to practice multilateralism. Kyrgyzstan's historic election as a nonpermanent member of the United Nations Security Council is a cause for celebration. It presents us with an opportunity to enhance coordination across the U.N., firmly uphold the U.N.-centered international system and the international order based on international law, act on the vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity and China's four global initiatives, unequivocally oppose hegemonism, unilateralism, and bloc confrontation, jointly combat terrorism, separatism, and extremism, and bring into play a more just and equitable global governance system. Over the past 25 years, the SCO has fostered and followed the Shanghai Spirit of mutual trust, mutual benefit, equality, consultation, respect for diversity of civilizations, and pursuit of common development. It has pioneered a new model of regional cooperation that features partnership instead of alliance, safeguards shared security and stability, and promotes common development and prosperity. It has become a comprehensive regional organization with the widest geographical coverage, the largest population, and enormous potential. Since taking over the SCO presidency, Kyrgyzstan has carried out a great deal of productive work. China commends Kyrgyzstan's efforts in building consensus among member states and advancing practical cooperation under the theme "Together Toward Sustainable Peace, Development, and Prosperity." China is convinced that with the concerted efforts of all sides, this year's SCO summit will be a crowning success and provide fresh impetus for carrying forward the Shanghai Spirit and building an SCO community with a shared future. Kyrgyzstan has a saying, "Drop by drop, a lake is formed." Likewise, we Chinese often say, "Without small streams, there would be no great rivers." China is ready to work with Kyrgyzstan to steadily advance our multifaceted cooperation, channel the streams of our people's goodwill into the river of our two nations' friendship, and jointly open up new prospects for the high-quality development of China-Kyrgyzstan relations. ■
